subject: Headroom fracture: LatticePay reserved throughput deficit and urgent exec alignment
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@latticepay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: OnyxCloud Ops <ops@onyxcloud.io>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden tail latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (LatticePay)

Hi Mina —

We started seeing a sustained tail-latency increase (~30-40% p95->p99) across our reserved endpoints at 08:40 PT and a correlated uptick in 5xx (mostly 503s) for about 20 minutes. Token throughput feels fine, but request queuing climbed quickly and a subset of requests timed out.

Attached is our latency snapshot and a short log excerpt. We rolled back a local model tweak and the error rate dropped but latency remains elevated for the last hour. Our customers are noticing degraded checkout times — this is impacting merchant SLAs.

Please advise next steps and whether you can open an emergency burst or reroute us to compatible capacity. If we have to throttle client calls, we need guidance on safe thresholds.

Alex
Alex Wu | CTO, LatticePay
alex.wu@latticepay.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: lattice_latency_report_20261026.pdf, ticket_4238_console_log.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@latticepay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (LatticePay)

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the artifacts. I’m escalating to support and ops immediately (cc'd David and Irene). High-level plan:

- Run a short triage to confirm if this is dedicated GPU headroom or a runtime regression.
- If pool saturation, propose a temporary remap to a compatible fallback model with slightly lower token cost to relieve headroom.
- If needed, request a 1-hour emergency burst (we'll need exec approval).

Can you confirm:
1) Typical QPS for the endpoints affected (last 2 hours).
2) Whether you changed any payload size / context windows in the last 4 hours.
3) If you want us to enable graceful throttling on your client key (we can suggest 10-15% backoff to reduce queuing).

Irene/David — initial telemetry attached shows a sharp GPU slot wait increase around 08:40. David, please validate KV-cache miss rates and confirm whether a model rebuild pushed new kernel selection that could increase per-token latency.

I'll keep Alex updated in-thread. Planning a 30-min ops bridge if we confirm saturation.

—Mina
Mina Haddad | Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/LP-4238

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (LatticePay)

Team — quick technical readout from infra:

- Observed: GPU headroom for LatticePay's dedicated pool dropped to ~4% at 08:38; queue depth spiked and token service started returning 503s when queue wait > configured SLO.
- Root signal: a pattern of increased KV-cache misses after a model parameter change earlier this morning (likely increased effective context window). More cache evictions -> more per-token memory pressure -> slower kernel paths on T4/RTX class nodes.
- Corroborated by OnyxCloud metrics (attached grafana snapshot).

Immediate mitigations we can enact within 20m:
1) Hot remap 30% of LatticePay traffic to the compatible 8-bit quantized variant (v3-compat-q8). Lower latency but slight quality delta.
2) Apply temporary per-key graceful backpressure (10% request cap) while remap finishes.
3) Request emergency burst: +6 reserved GPUs for 1 hour (to absorb the cache-warmup storm) — requires sales/exec signoff for short-term allocation and potential credit.

If Marissa approves burst, I’ll coordinate the pod scale and route remap. Post-incident, we should add a guardrail: runtime kernel-change can auto-suggest a burst + cache-warmup window for reserved customers.

Attachments: grafana_gpu_headroom_20261026.png, ticket_4238_console_log.txt

-David
David Kim | Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 07:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency + 5xx spike on reserved pool (LatticePay)

Thanks for the concise summary. I’m authorizing a one-hour emergency burst (up to 6 GPUs) for LatticePay to stabilize service while we execute the remap and cache warm-up. Please proceed with:

- David: enact remap to v3-compat-q8 immediately and enable a 10% graceful backoff on the key. Coordinate scale with infra and confirm when traffic is shifted.
- Mina: notify Alex of the approval and confirm whether LatticePay wants transient credits or a formal one-off credit request to be handled by finance.
- Irene: loop in CSM and Legal; if this becomes a contractual SLA hole we need a customer-friendly remediation note and a path to avoid recurrence.

After stabilization, I want a short postmortem within 48 hours covering: why kernel selection change caused cache-flush sensitivity, what telemetry we add to detect this earlier, and a proposed product guardrail (auto-burst + warmup or scheduled kernel change cooldown).

Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0210
